title: ops-bridge-comm-protocols-and-template-bundle
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight pocket playbook for the on-call bridge lead and SRE responders focused exclusively on communications: status page messages, customer-facing messages (two tones), and the internal war-room checklist.

How to use:
- Use the three-tier status templates below (Initial / Ongoing / Resolved) verbatim for the status page; edit placeholders only.
- Pick the customer-facing template that matches the customer tier (Enterprise or Self-serve).
- Follow the internal war-room checklist immediately after bridge creation to stabilize the signal and coordinate updates.
- Use Slack templates for quick pings to owners and execs.

Severity buckets and comm expectations:
- Sev 1 (P0): Customer-facing within 10 minutes; status page up within 15 minutes; cadence: 15m updates.
- Sev 2 (P1): Status page within 30 minutes; cadence: 30–60m updates.
- Sev 3 (P2): Status page optional; one initial update and a final resolution note.

Status page templates (copy/paste and replace names/times):
1) INITIAL — short, public, plain-language
Status: Investigating
Summary: We are investigating reports of increased error rates for the Redwood hosted inference API in us-west-2. Some requests are failing with 5xx errors.
Impact: Some customers may see increased latency or failed requests for text generation endpoints. We are actively investigating and will provide an update within 15 minutes.
Next update: <HH:MM UTC>
Incident ID: <INCIDENT-YYYY-MM-DD-#>

2) ONGOING — factual, progress-oriented
Status: Partial degradation
Summary: Our engineering team has isolated the issue to a degraded routing layer affecting a subset of inference workers. We have routed traffic away from affected pools and are validating fallbacks.
Impact: Approximately X% of requests to models in the us-west-2 region are impacted; customers using pinned Dedicated pools are unaffected.
What we are doing: Rebalancing traffic, restarting affected hosts, and running a targeted KV cache flush to restore steady-state.
Next update: <HH:MM UTC> or sooner if there is a material change.
Mitigation: Automatic fallback to compatible model variants is active for most customers; if you still experience failures, please contact support with your request IDs.

3) RESOLVED — concise, root-cause direction optional
Status: Resolved
Summary: The routing layer degradation was caused by an incremental control-plane rollout. Rolling back the rollout and rebalancing hosts restored service.
Impact: Customers in us-west-2 experienced elevated failure rates between <start> and <end>. No data loss.
What we did: Rolled back the rollout, restarted affected workers, verified request success rates, and monitored KPIs for 2 hours post-fix.
Follow-up: A post-incident review (PIR) is scheduled. Affected customers will receive an email summary within 48 hours.

Customer-facing templates
- Enterprise (formal, empathetic, actionable):
Subject: Incident update — Redwood inference service (region: us-west-2)
Hi <Customer Name>,
We wanted to let you know that we recently experienced an interruption affecting inference requests in us-west-2. Our operations team investigated and deployed mitigations that restored service at <end time UTC>.
Impact: You may have observed increased latency or failed requests between <start time> and <end time>.
Action for you: No action required unless you continue to observe errors. If you do, please reply to this message with sample request IDs and timestamps and we will prioritize a review.
Our commitment: We understand this may have affected production traffic and we apologize for the disruption. We are performing a full post-incident review and will share findings and any recommended changes within 48 hours.
Sincerely,
Redwood Inference — Customer Reliability Team

- Self-serve / Developer (short, frank, pragmatic):
Subject: Service interruption — Redwood API (us-west-2)
Quick note: We experienced increased failures for some API requests in us-west-2 between <start> and <end>. We rolled back the change and traffic is healthy now.
If you saw errors: retrying should succeed; consider increasing client-side retries for transient 5xx in the short term. If you have persistent problems, paste request IDs into a support ticket.
Thanks for bearing with us — we’ll post a brief PIR soon.

Internal war-room checklist (first 30 minutes) — bridge leader responsibilities:
1) Bridge and context
- Create a dedicated bridge channel (zoom/meet + private Slack channel).
- Summon on-call owners: serving-runtime lead, infra owner, routing engineer, SRE on-call, and the on-call support rep.
- Tag exec-oncall only after first 15 minutes unless customer impact escalates.

2) Triage snapshot (collect and share on the bridge):
- Key metrics: error-rate (5xx), p50/p95 latency, success-rate by model, percent of traffic routed to fallback.
- Example query lines (share raw IDs): latest 50 failed request IDs and sample stack traces.
- Known changes: any recent rollouts, infra changes, config pushes in last 60 minutes.

3) Immediate mitigations (pick one):
- Rollback the last control-plane rollout.
- Route traffic away from affected availability zones or hosts.
- Apply circuit-breaker to degraded model variant.
- Increase autoscale/burst capacity as emergency buffer.

4) Communications cadence (delegate):
- Scribe: document actions and timestamps in the incident doc live.
- Public comm: post initial status page item (bridge lead).
- Customer comm: assign owner for enterprise customers (account rep + solutions eng).
- Engineering updates: every 15m for P0, 30–60m for P1.

5) Stabilization checklist (first 2 hours):
- Verify end-to-end success rates across models and regions.
- Confirm fallback behaviors and cache consistency.
- Run synthetic smoke tests from multiple regions.

Slack quick-templates (paste into bridge channel):
- Ping to owner: @owner — incident <INCID> created for elevated 5xx in us-west-2. Can you validate whether the last control-plane rollout touched routing service?
- Exec ping (use sparingly): @exec-oncall — P0 in us-west-2, impact on hosted API. Initial mitigation: rollback initiated. Next update in 15m.

Post-incident review prompts (to include in PIR):
- Timeline: minute-by-minute timeline from alert -> detection -> mitigation -> resolution.
- Detection gap: how long between first error and on-call awareness?
- RCA focus: causal chain (change -> failure mode -> why safeguards failed).
- Action items: owner, target date, verification steps, and risk mitigation plan to prevent recurrence.
- Customer outreach: list of customers contacted and draft copies of emails sent.

Comms hygiene rules (do not forget):
- Never speculate about unconfirmed root causes in public messages.
- If there is possible customer data impact, escalate immediately to legal/compliance and security.
- Keep status page language simple, avoid technical acronyms without brief explanation.

Templates repository and ownership:
- This doc is intentionally compact; canonical templates live in Confluence: confluence://sre/incident-comm-templates.
- Ops-bridge comms ownership: eng-sre (on-call rotation). PRs for templates: open a PR against the canonical Confluence page and notify eng-sre.

Appendix: quick checklist for support engineers handling inbound tickets:
- Ask for request ID, timestamp, model, and region.
- Verify whether the request timestamp falls inside the incident window.
- If inside window, create a high-priority follow-up and add to incident doc. Provide ETA for customer response.
- If outside, escalate to normal support flow and close with reproduction steps.

Notes and open questions:
- Consider adding a one-click status page composer in the console to reduce cadence friction.
- Discuss retention window for incident emails: 48 hours for initial summary, 7 days for follow-up PIR notification.

End of doc.
